votes.evidence:
Checked at bc7090d. In src/listing/load.ts, loadPluginDir (about lines 172-202) reads only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, the README, the LICENSE and the package-manager configs. It never resolves a string `mcpServers` path for a Claude plugin. The only code that resolves a declared path is declaredMcp (about line 236), and only the OpenAI manifest uses it. That code came from round-3 fix A06-09, which covered ChatGPT/OpenAI only, so this is not a known item.

In src/rules/listing.ts, pluginServers (lines 39-48) collects servers only from `.mcp.json` and from inline object or array entries in plugin.json. pluginServerRefs (lines 51-54) returns the string entries, and only LST-010 uses it, which acts only on `.mcpb`/`.dxt`. LST-006, LST-007, LST-008, LST-009 (through pluginServers) and LST-011 all iterate pluginServers. So a server in a referenced `.json` file is never checked, and nothing reports that the file was skipped or that a path such as `../` leaves the plugin folder.

I reproduced it in a detached worktree with a fresh build. I used a copy of plugin-valid without `.mcp.json`, with `mcpServers: "./servers.json"` pointing at an `npx` unpinned server whose env holds a `ghp_` token. The result was 0 errors, 0 warnings, PASS, exit 0. With `["../outside.json"]` the result was also PASS with nothing reported.

Severity: I rate it medium, not high. It is a silent false negative for a documented but less common way to declare servers: it can turn a directory blocker into a PASS, but it never raises a false error. Round 3 rated the similar silent-fallback case for OpenAI, A06-09, as low. Expected fix: read the referenced `.json` files into pluginServers, and report a missing or outside path as "not checked" (a warning).

The worktree was removed afterwards.

Code at bc7090d: loadPluginDir (src/listing/load.ts ~172-200) reads only .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the root .mcp.json. pluginServers (src/rules/listing.ts:39-48) collects only .mcp.json and inline object/array-of-object mcpServers. String refs go only to pluginServerRefs, which is used only at listing.ts:504-509 (LST-010 bundle .mcpb/.dxt). No rule checks a '..' path in plugin.json mcpServers; the 'outside' handling at :1021 covers images only. Built the CLI in a detached worktree and ran it on a copy of plugin-valid. (1) .mcp.json removed, plugin.json "mcpServers": "./servers.json", servers.json = {"mcpServers":{"x":{"command":"npx","args":["some-unpinned-pkg"],"env":{"API_TOKEN":"ghp_<36>"}}}}: output was 0 errors, 0 warnings, "Claude: NO AUTOMATED BLOCKERS · Result: PASS", exit 0, with no note that servers.json was not read. (2) Control with the same content placed in .mcp.json: 2 errors (LST-008, LST-011), BLOCKED. (3) "mcpServers": ["../outside.json"]: 0 errors, 0 warnings, PASS. So two Blocks-level errors (LST-008, LST-011) are lost when the plugin uses a documented form of mcpServers, and the verdict is a false PASS. That justifies high severity for the missed detection. Possible fixes: read the referenced ./ .json files inside the plugin and feed them to pluginServers. For a ref that cannot be read or points outside the plugin, report an error, or at least a warning that it was not checked. I did not re-fetch the plugins reference page; the doc quote is taken from the finding. Side note, outside this finding: the control run printed the line "Need help getting your connector approved? 20horizon93@gmail.com" in the CLI output. This looks worth a separate check. Worktree removed.
